name: Storyboard and hooks
summary: Plan a 28 s or 16 s card before drawing it: beat sheets, 14 tested hook patterns, a pacing checklist and a storyboard.json that compiles into a timeline.
qualityBar: Both beat templates add up to T minus the 3.1 s closer, hook first and payoff last
14 hook patterns whose examples fit at 88 px or more with no banned claim and no hype word; banned, hype, price, over-long and empty hooks are caught
Voice-time model within 0.25 s mean and 1.0 s worst over 95 measured Kokoro script rows (in-sample fit; 0.17 s held-out)
Both example storyboards compile deterministically and pass all 14 pacing checks
17 deliberately broken storyboards each fail the check that names their fault
makeCard returns a working 1080x1920 frame function; demo 7.5 s, silent, QC pass, every number on screen from the compiler
verifiedBy: 2026-11-19: node test.mjs exit 0 at full size (121 checks passed, 0 failed; demo 1080x1920, 7.5 s, silent; engine QC passed). The pacing checker caught a real fault in my own first example (a proof-beat voice line 0.11 s too long) which I then fixed. I viewed a 12-frame sheet of the demo (beat sheet page, timeline with playhead and novelty curve, four ticked checks, closer) and judged it good. NOT checked: whether these rules actually raise viewer retention (the thresholds are habits taken from the tt10 standard and common short-video practice, not measured on BGI's own audience data); the hook patterns were not tested with viewers; the voice-time model is fitted to Kokoro Heart only; no audio; the novelty curve is the plan restated, not a forecast.
